en.text: The Governor of a state is appointed by the [[1]] and holds office during the [[2]] of the President. Under Article [[3]], the Governor may give assent to a bill, withhold assent and return it to the legislature, or reserve it for the President. The Governor's power to grant pardons for offences under state law is in Article [[4]].
en.why: Article 72 is the President's pardoning power; the Governor's is Article 161. "Pleasure" is the key word: the Governor has no fixed security of tenure.

hi.text: राज्य के राज्यपाल की नियुक्ति [[1]] करते हैं और वे राष्ट्रपति के [[2]] तक पद पर रहते हैं। अनुच्छेद [[3]] के तहत राज्यपाल किसी विधेयक पर अनुमति दे सकते हैं, अनुमति रोककर उसे विधानमंडल को लौटा सकते हैं या राष्ट्रपति के लिए आरक्षित कर सकते हैं। राज्य कानून के अपराधों में क्षमा देने की राज्यपाल की शक्ति अनुच्छेद [[4]] में है।
hi.why: अनुच्छेद 72 राष्ट्रपति की क्षमादान शक्ति है; राज्यपाल की अनुच्छेद 161 में है। "प्रसादपर्यंत" मुख्य शब्द है: राज्यपाल के कार्यकाल की कोई निश्चित सुरक्षा नहीं है।

sources.en: Constitution of India, Articles 155, 156, 161 and 200; Supreme Court of India, Special Reference No. 1 of 2025, opinion of 20 November 2025

factsToCheck: Article 200 options as read in the Presidential reference opinion (Special Reference No. 1 of 2025, five-judge bench, unanimous, 20 November 2025): assent, withhold assent and return the bill under the first proviso, or reserve it for the President. Withholding without returning is not an option. The opinion also held that courts cannot set timelines and that there is no 'deemed assent', but prolonged unexplained inaction can be reviewed in a limited way. It departed from State of Tamil Nadu v. Governor of Tamil Nadu (two-judge bench, 8 April 2025) on timelines and deemed assent. Timelines are not used in this file
